name: Renaissance painting
summary: A picture as a measured window onto the world: linear perspective, modelled figures, a stable geometry and a calm, idealised body. Florentine and Venetian workshops and Flemish oil painters set the rules.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture is a window onto a measured space, and the ideal human body is the measure of that space.
design_principles: Set one vanishing point on the horizon line, at 40–50% of the picture height, and make every orthogonal converge on it.
Arrange the main figures in a triangle or pyramid, with the apex on the centre axis in the upper third.
Model each form with a smooth gradation from light to shade in 6–8 steps, with no drawn outline on the flesh.
Build colour in thin glazes over a drawn underlayer, and level the surface until no stroke is visible.
Put a calm landscape or a piece of architecture behind the figures, and make it cooler, paler and bluer with each step of distance.
Place the horizon, the focal figure and the architecture on the golden section or on a 2:3 ratio.
Pose figures in contrapposto with the head turned 10–30° from the shoulders, and give the hands a meaning.
anti_patterns: Visible brush strokes on figures or faces
Diagonal compositions with a single hard beam of light
Elongated limbs, twisted poses or a stretched neck
Figures cropped by the picture edge
Fully saturated colour over more than a robe or two

composition.layout: A pyramid of figures on a symmetric or near-symmetric plan, inside a perspective box with a visible floor grid of 8–12 squares.
composition.focal_point: The head of the central figure sits on the vertical centre axis or within 10% of it, at 30–40% of the height from the top.
composition.format: Portrait panels at 2:3 or 3:4 for devotional work; landscape 3:2 for narrative. Figures stay 5–10% inside the edges.

principles.rule: Hold a central axis with a bilateral balance within 10% of equal visual weight left and right.
Use the golden section (1:1.618) for the horizon, the focal head and the main architectural division.
Use three planes: figures in the front 40%, architecture or terrace in the middle, a pale blue landscape in the last 20%.
Direct every gaze, gesture and orthogonal toward one head or one hand.

palette.strategy: Local colour that is rich but controlled: one great blue, one red, earth tones and a pale sky; harmony from glazed transparency, not from contrast.
palette.distribution: Earth and flesh tones 45%, muted green and sky 30%, white and gold 15%, the strong blue and red together under 10%.
palette.ground: White gesso on poplar panel with a thin warm imprimatura of 5–10% umber.

colours.name: Ultramarine
colours.role: robe of the Virgin, the strongest chroma

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Egg tempera for the underpainting, then oil glazes; or oil alone in Flanders.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Poplar panel with gesso, 10–40mm thick; later canvas in Venice.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Small, hidden strokes; no visible stroke wider than 3mm inside a figure.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: Thin layers of 10–30 microns, built from a drawn underpainting by hatching and glaze; impasto only in jewellery and gold highlights.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Soft edges inside forms and a firm edge only at the contour of the main figure; the faces are blended by sfumato.

light_and_modelling.light: One soft source from the upper left at about 45°, diffuse, as in a room with a north window.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Smooth gradation from light to dark in 6–8 steps; highlights small, cool and placed on the forehead, nose and knuckles.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Transparent shadows in brown-green; no black, and shadow covers 25–35% of each form.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Warm flesh and drapery in the foreground against cool blue-green distance.

subject.typical: Madonna and Child, saints, three-quarter portraits, mythological allegory, the ideal city.
subject.figure_scale: Figures fill 50–70% of the picture height; the head is 1/7 to 1/8 of the body height.
subject.treatment: Idealised faces and bodies with calm expressions; narrative shown at its quietest moment.

surface.finish: Smooth and glossy, like enamel, with all brush marks levelled and a clear resin varnish.
surface.texture: Fine, even panel without visible grain; at most a hairline craquelure.

works.work: Virgin and Child with an Angel
Virgin and Child with Two Angels

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). Look at the museum page for the image and its licence.

emotion.target_response: Calm and order: the viewer trusts a world that someone has measured and found harmonious.

avoid_when: The brief asks for motion, drama or visible gesture.
The subject is modern urban life, or the picture must read as flat graphic design.

modifiers.how: Keep the perspective and the modelled figures; replace the diffuse light with one hard source, move the focal point off the axis, and darken the shadows to 50–60% of the area.
Keep the outdoor setting and the cool distance; drop the underdrawing, break each form into visible strokes 5–15mm wide and remove the outline.
